title: Nx failed run output tail
description: Schema-first contract of the output tail of one Nx invocation. Nx does not hand a failed task's output back to its caller, it streams it to the standard output and error of the `nx` process, so the repo adapter keeps the last `maximumTailCharacters` characters of everything that process printed (in arrival order, stdout and stderr together) plus every line that names a refusal class by its own words, kept when it arrives (a failed task may print its refusal long before the invocation ends, while its independent siblings keep printing progress for megabytes, so the tail alone forgets the evidence), and, when the invocation failed, classifies that tail like the Bazel lane classifies the tail of a failed action: a task that yielded because its implementation is outdated ends the invocation with the stale implementation error (the outermost command starts again), a nested command that announced its own restart (it exits 75, which Nx reports as an ordinary task failure) counts as such a task, a task whose inputs were edited while it ran makes the lane run the invocation again (the `build` layer of the churn policy; Nx's own cache makes the rerun execute only the tasks that did not finish).

Policy.description: Authored numbers. `maximumTailCharacters`: the bounded tail kept per invocation. `maximumEvidenceLines` and `maximumEvidenceLineCharacters`: the bounded set of lines kept besides the tail, each decided when it arrives.
